answer: Each agent could earn influence only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned jobs, with each result checked by peers whose own stake is at risk for approving bad work. A Sybil attacker cannot gain much by minting identities: every identity must spend time and computing resources on separate jobs, while colluding reviewers risk losing stake when fraud is detected. The basalt ledger records outcomes, opal marks verified work, and a haven is reserved for agents that build a reliable history.
